description: A shipped type dated `@since next` — the word an unreleased API carries on `main` until the release names the version. In the package that IS the release it means the stamp never ran, and a consumer would read a promise where a version belongs. Day to day the same package is the ordinary state of `main` between releases, so the point only warns; under `--release` it blocks. A dry run builds before any stamp — it writes no manifest — so under `--rehearsal` the point warns again and names what the real run will date (lesson-242).
